summary: Provisioning's own `jj git clone`/`jj git fetch` now run with the clone's credential-helper chain reset and `credential.interactive=true`, through five `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment pairs added in `createProvisioningCredential` (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`) — the one env both the daemon host's provisioning and the pod's `legion workspace-init` hand to jj. The persisted clone config (pane helper on both keys, `credential.interactive=false`) is unchanged. PR sjawhar/legion#1121, code head c336112cf94f52e73b948c4cbab3903cce260a7c, review round 1 answered at 8e89ad9efc83bc56eaa5fb0944fa03faed1c33b5 (tests and doc comments only); Worker Image digest sha256:ba1b024282b5e2c0db1c5ab4dad17b4b4a6e07582b9aea7f3dc0972b33a6060d.

trickyParts: Bun 1.3.14 `toMatchObject` fails an asymmetric matcher (`expect.stringContaining`) on the second match of the same object reference — provisioning hands the clone and the fetch one shared `credential.env` object, so workspace-init.test.ts asserts GIT_ASKPASS apart from the plain-value `toMatchObject` (comment in the test).

The `test` CI job failed once on a real-tmux flake (`processes.test.ts` deployment-instructions case: `tmux window ownership marker failed (exit 1): server exited unexpectedly`, 1653/1654 pass) unrelated to this PR; re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun 34938845488 --failed`, no new commit.

Dispatch `POST /api/v1/issues` and PATCH with a bearer require `actor: {kind: session, id}`; the listener's `/v1/messages/publish` requires a `message` field beside `payload` — both learned by 400 during the relay and fixed in the run's relay script.

The hard kill (`kill -9 -1; kill -9 1` inside the worker container) produced a real death: no `/process/exit`, the resync probe found the pod Failed and resurrected the same session — the re-admission fallback in the plan was not needed.

Review round 1: `git config --get-all` concatenates every scope, so a test reading a clone's persisted helpers must pin GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM (or use --local); the fills already did, the reads did not. Reproduced with a scratch GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, never the box's real global config.
archaeology: The replaced pin `expect(env.GIT_CONFIG_COUNT).toBeUndefined()` (workspace.test.ts `provisioningEnv`) came from PR #753's squash 9278a29c, sub-commit b0c456b5 'feat(legion): add verified smoke rig and delivery gates' — the same commit that introduced createProvisioningCredential and the askpass design; it read as 'provisioning hands git no inline config; the token travels only through the askpass script'. The new contract (PROVISIONING_ENV_NAMES: exactly eight names, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 empty, the token only in LEGION_PROVISIONING_TOKEN) keeps the second half and replaces the first with the five exact pairs; the pinned-helper test's pane env `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: "0"` models a pane and stays.
deviations: None from the plan's fix contract. Read-only `bunx biome check` was run on the four TypeScript files this PR touches (not project-wide, no --write) to avoid burning a CI round on a formatting miss; it found one over-long line in the new test, wrapped by hand.

changes: BLOCKING: workspace.test.ts `persisted()` runs its `git config --get-all/--get` reads under the test's isolation env (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, fixture HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME) instead of inheriting the box's global and system scopes.

(a) `provisioningEnv` and the workspace-init.test.ts block are one `toEqual` each with an asymmetric matcher on GIT_ASKPASS (exact key set kept; PROVISIONING_ENV_NAMES removed); the in-test negative control is built positively as the pre-LEGION-178 env.
(b) the `git --version` read moved from module level into the one test that prints it.
(c) the archaeology citation names the squash 9278a29c instead of the pre-squash b0c456b5.
(d) `processEnvRunner`'s doc comment names the GIT_CONFIG_* pairs and `createProvisioningCredential`.
No change to workspace.ts, processes.ts, the workflow, or the docs; c336112c and the handoff commits were not rewritten.
